more: QBs in round 1: none in 2021, which was a 1QB draft (the league voted in superflex a month after it, on June 1, 2021). In 2022, the first superflex draft, Kenny Pickett went 1.08. Three QBs went 1.02–1.04 in 2023, then five in round 1 in 2024 (Caleb, Daniels, Maye, McCarthy, Nix). All nine first-round QBs came from superflex drafts.
The 2021 QBs taken in round 3 (Fields, Lance, Zach Wilson, Mac Jones) were 1QB-format picks, so they were cheap for a reason.
1.07 is the unlucky slot: 1 of 4 hit (Bateman, Olave, Quentin Johnston, McCarthy), then TreVeyon Henderson in 2025. Picks 1.02, 1.04 and 1.05 are 4 for 4.
First TE taken each year: Pitts 1.03 (2021), McBride 3.06 (2022), then the end of round 1 every year since (Kincaid, Bowers, Warren, Sadiq at 1.08–1.10).
The 2021 class has scored the most (21,176 career points). The 2025 class is worth the most (134,372 KTC), ahead of 2026 (127,983).
Hit rate by position, all years: TE 43%, RB 36%, QB 29%, WR 21%. WRs are drafted the most (114 picks) and hit the least.
13 players from the 2021–25 classes have scored fewer than 5 career points.
